posts.content_md:
I am reposting here as I would like to try to keep discussions to a minimum in the Tips and Tricks section as asked.

I am sorry for not being totally complete. If anyone has ever had a laser pointer and is using any type of laser to make a hologram I assumed the obvious would not need to be stated. Yes the laser beam should be expanded with almost any type of lens and then can be shone on the wall near the area needed to lit. 

I had two. One I used as described above and another as a "Safe Flashlight". I could carry around. I used a plastic lens (quality does not matter) that I taped right on the pointer. I kept the pointer with its batteries and this allowed me carry the pointer around and shine the light wherever additional lighting was need without any worry of fogging plates.

> **Dinesh:** I just use standard 25W bulbs with solid, as opposed to transparent, glass

I personally stayed away from using any type of "standard" light bulbs with VRP emulsion. I actually did not know a standard light bulb chould be used with VRP without a filter.

posts.content_md:
Works fine. Slavich is too insensitive to worry about fogging as much as I needed to with Agfa. I don't know how much you used VRP, but I've been using it for the last 5 years here: [http://www.dragonseye.com/holography/PC ... 0_2085.JPG](http://www.dragonseye.com/holography/PCGGII/thumbs/120_2085.JPG)

and, as you can see, it's only a bulb in a socket (top right in picture).

That's good info. I only used VRP for a short while (less then a box), and remembering the Agfa didn't want to take chances.

Do you use that light just for processing or in the table room for loading the plate also. How long do you think (approximately) the plate can be exposed to that type/quantity of radiation before it starts to fog?

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
I guess what I am driving at is not a particular and precisely measure time but more along the lines of... and this is just an example....

I only use the light to put the plate in the plate holder, which is only a minute or so. Then I keep the room pitch black. Then after the exposure I use the light but only for the few minutes until developing is done. This would indicate a few minutes is ok but 20 minutes in this type of light may be too much. Just curious!!!
